findings.title: Access-token matcher logic inverted and wrong offset
findings.body: In isAccessTokenId the check is `if (items[0].substring(3, 5).equals(expectedGrantShortcut)) return false;`. This is backwards: it rejects tokens whose grant shortcut matches and accepts tokens whose shortcut differs. It also uses substring(3,5) while the documented layout is 2 chars session + 2 chars token-type + 2 chars grant, so the grant lives at substring(4,6). As a result expectCodeToToken / expectRefresh / expectDeviceCodeToToken / expectAuthReqIdToToken will pass for wrong grants and fail for correct grants.

findings.title: Constructor validates grantType twice, never rawTokenId
findings.body: The constructor contains `Objects.requireNonNull(grantType, "Null grantType not allowed"); Objects.requireNonNull(grantType, "Null rawTokenId not allowed");`. The second check should be on rawTokenId. A null rawTokenId is therefore accepted and later concatenated into `... + ':' + getRawTokenId()` producing an id ending in "null" or an NPE far from the cause, while the error message is misleading.

findings.title: Removal of Context copy-constructor breaks custom grants
findings.body: The diff deletes the public `Context(Context context)` copy constructor and adds a new required `grantType` field initialized from formParams. Any third-party OAuth2GrantType implementation that copied/cloned the context via `new Context(context)` no longer compiles, and subclasses that constructed a Context in another way get a different semantic. This is an incompatible SPI break; the old constructor should be retained (deprecated) and delegate to the new logic.

findings.title: Blind cast to OAuth2GrantTypeFactory can throw ClassCastException
findings.body: postInit (and getGrantTypeByShortcut) does `OAuth2GrantTypeFactory gtf = (OAuth2GrantTypeFactory) factory1;` for every factory from `getProviderFactoriesStream(OAuth2GrantType.class)`. A custom OAuth2GrantType whose factory does not implement the extended OAuth2GrantTypeFactory interface (compiled against the old SPI that had no getShortcut) will cause a ClassCastException at server startup, preventing boot. An instanceof check / graceful fallback is required.

findings.title: Malformed token IDs throw instead of falling back to UNKNOWN
findings.body: getTokenContextFromTokenId throws IllegalArgumentException when the prefix before ':' is not exactly 6 chars or contains an unknown shortcut. Tokens issued before this feature have no prefix and are handled, but any token with a ':' and unexpected prefix (custom encoder, corrupted jti, foreign issuer, shortcut longer than 2 chars) will now throw out of the decode path instead of returning SessionType.UNKNOWN/TokenType.UNKNOWN. Since token IDs come from the network (introspection, userinfo, revocation), this turns bad input into unhandled 500s.
